rv.q: What this piece needs is a substantial story, but Owen gives us little insight into the characters, or any sense of them responding to the sociopolitical tremors gripping the city at the time.
When all is said and sung, Blaemire (Glory Days, Space Dogs), who wrote the book, music, and lyrics, has created a mixed bag of a musical.
The experience of watching this show is engaging, and it’s packed full of metaphor and meaning while also maintaining a plot that is easy to follow.
Soon grapples with both the existential and practical side of dying. But its perspective on living rarely resonates emotionally.
If one appears, grab it. I won't tell you what happens behind Charlie's closed door. I will only tell you that when Soon finally opens it, it is heartbreaking in the best possible way.
The trees may be ablaze, but this is Manhattan, so groceries can still be ordered, and thus romance finds its way into Charlie’s homestead.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this intimate pop musical about climate anxiety and isolation, with praise for its honest emotional core but criticism for its thin narrative and unclear focus.
